text.p: Belgium's Generale Bank said on Thursday it upgraded its rating on shares in polyurethane foam maker Recticel SA to 'hold', while broker Vermeulen Raemdonck/BBL upgraded it to 'buy'.

Generale Bank said it upgraded its recommendation to 'hold' from 'sell' after Recticel announced late on Wednesday a 1996 group loss of 38 million Belgian francs, in line with the bank's forecast. This compared to a 1995 loss of 682 million francs.
"More importantly, cash flow increased from 0.8 billion francs to 1.4 billion, slightly better than we anticipated," the bank said in a research note.
The bank noted that Recticel management expected the improvement witnessed during second-half of 1996 to continue into 1997, provided raw material prices remained stable.

"As the production problems for dashboards in the automotive division are under control now and as new contracts confirm management's confidence in this activity, our recommendation for (Recticel) share is upgraded to 'hold'", it said.
Vermeulen Raemdonck said, "1996 results show a better than expected second-half. The positive earnings surprise leads us to upgrade our recommendation to speculative buy."
Vermeulen Raemdonck said it revised its earning per share estimate for 1997 upwards to 20 francs from 11 francs.
